metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.note: Four items to classify: copper coin (conductor), plastic (insulator), glass (insulator), aluminium can (conductor). 4 slots × 0.5m each = 2m. Modelled as drag-to-label: each item dragged to CONDUCTOR or INSULATOR. Word bank has 2 labels (repeated) — students assign each item to a label.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q4a — Classify Conductors and Insulators
question.text:
Classify each of the following materials as a conductor or insulator of electricity by dragging the correct label into each blank:

MaterialConductor or Insulator?
Copper coin[[1]]
Plastic[[2]]
Glass[[3]]
Aluminium can[[4]]
question.general_feedback:
Conductors (allow current to flow — have free electrons):

  • Copper coin — copper is a metal, excellent conductor
  • Aluminium can — aluminium is a metal, good conductor

Insulators (do not allow current to flow — no free electrons):

  • Plastic — polymer; electrons tightly bound in covalent bonds
  • Glass — covalent/ionic amorphous solid; no free charge carriers at room temperature

groups.label: Copper coin
groups.diagnostic_hint: Copper is a metal. All metals have delocalised (free) electrons that move through the structure and carry charge — so copper is a conductor.

groups.label: Plastic
groups.diagnostic_hint: Plastic is a polymer where all electrons are tightly bound in covalent bonds — no free charge carriers. Plastic is an insulator.

groups.label: Glass
groups.diagnostic_hint: Glass is an amorphous solid (covalent/ionic network). At room temperature it has no free electrons or ions to carry charge — glass is an insulator. (Note: graphite is a non-metal that IS a conductor — don't confuse hard solids with conductors.)

groups.label: Aluminium can
groups.diagnostic_hint: Aluminium is a metal with free electrons in a delocalised sea — it conducts electricity. Aluminium is widely used in electrical wiring and transmission lines.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 2 reusable tokens for 4 slots. Conductors: Copper coin (slot 1), Aluminium can (slot 4). Insulators: Plastic (slot 2), Glass (slot 3). A binary DDWTOS — students learn the rule that metals are conductors. The key challenge is glass, which some students confuse with graphite (which IS a conductor) or assume all hard materials conduct.
